narrative.overview: A small, well-made measuring device on a workbench: anodised black, warm paper, one signal orange. The instrument measures; the paper records. The reference is Teenage Engineering's OP-1 field / TX-6 language — palette, technical labelling, density and one signature move, not a costume of hardware controls. The type is Vercel's Geist family: Sans for prose, Mono for every number, Pixel for the mark and wordmark. The signature move is the printed receipt, which is also the share card.
keyCharacteristics: Paper documents and anodised device panels, never the same surface twice.
One signal orange used for live state, data and interaction — not decoration.
Mono numerals and technical labels; Sans prose; Pixel only as a mark.
Hairline rules, tight corners, flat colour, one soft shadow on the floating device.
The printed receipt is the brand artifact and the share action.

rules.name: The Paper/Device Rule
rules.body: Documents are paper with ink text; instruments are ink panels with paper text. Do not invert them for fashion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal orange is reserved for live data, the meter, focus and primary interaction. It never becomes a background wash, a gradient, or a second decorative accent.

rules.name: The Small Orange Rule
rules.body: On paper, small orange text uses Signal Orange Ink, display numerals use Signal Orange Display, and bright signal orange is reserved for graphics and ink fields.

rules.name: The Mono Measures Rule
rules.body: Every number, unit, serial, timestamp and technical label is Geist Mono. Prose is never mono; measurement is never proportional.

rules.name: The Pixel Is a Mark Rule
rules.body: Geist Pixel Square may draw the T mark or a wordmark at 18px or larger. It never sets body copy, small labels, or numbers.

rules.name: The Single Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it is not the floating HUD (or its collapsed orb), it does not cast a shadow. No glass, no blur, no coloured halos.

rules.name: The Tight Corner Rule
rules.body: Radii stay under 12px except the orb. If a rectangle needs 16px to feel friendly, the composition is doing the work wrong.

dos: Do keep documents paper and instruments ink; use the 1px hairline as the main divider.
Do set every number and technical label in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do use Signal Orange for live state, data, focus and one primary action.
Do keep the receipt's serial, barcode and dashed perforation.
Do self-host Geist and preserve the OFL licence.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass, backdrop blur, neon glows or coloured halos.
Don't add a second accent colour or reintroduce lime/violet.
Don't set body copy or small labels in Geist Pixel.
Don't put bright Signal Orange on paper for small text or display numerals.
Don't use cards inside cards, section numbers, eyebrow labels or emoji icons.
Don't animate everything; the receipt print and the two-step thinking blink are the only authored motions.
